title: Within-group and between-group covariance decomposition
purpose: Split the covariance between a score Y and a prediction P into the expected within-group covariance and the covariance of group means, exactly, using rational arithmetic. Use it to see whether a correlation comes from differences between tasks or sources rather than from agreement inside each group.

entry_points.name: decompose_covariance
entry_points.arguments: y, p: equal-length lists of numbers; groups: one text or integer label per row
entry_points.returns: {total_covariance, within_group, between_group, identity_residual, total_correlation, within_share, between_share, sign_conflict, groups}

assumptions: Moments are population moments (divide by n) with empirical group weights n_g / n; this is what makes the identity exact.
Each row belongs to exactly one group.
guarantees: total_covariance = within_group + between_group exactly in rational arithmetic on the exact binary values of the inputs; identity_residual is 0.0.
One group gives between_group 0; one row per group gives within_group 0.
Results are rounded to float only at the end.

known_wrong.name: within_part_is_not_the_total
known_wrong.why: Averaging the per-group covariances drops the between-group term; here it reports 1 while the overall covariance is 0.

limits: Population moments only; sample (n - 1) moments do not satisfy the identity. Rational arithmetic is exact but slow for very long inputs (tens of thousands of rows are fine). The decomposition describes the data at hand; it does not say which grouping is causally relevant, and correlations themselves do not decompose additively.
